questions.question: Who became the first woman to command the Armed Forces Transfusion Centre, Delhi Cantt, which is the largest blood transfusion centre of the Armed Forces in Nov 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Col Sunita BS**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Col Sunita BS** became the first woman to command the Armed Forces Transfusion Centre (AFTC) in Delhi Cantt in **November 2023**.
 
• The **Armed Forces Transfusion Centre** is the largest blood transfusion centre of the Indian Armed Forces, playing a crucial role in providing blood and its components for military personnel.
 
• Col Sunita BS has a distinguished career in **transfusion medicine** and has contributed significantly to improving blood collection and storage processes in the Armed Forces.
 
• This landmark achievement aligns with the Armed Forces' efforts to promote **gender equality** and increase women's representation in leadership roles.
 
• The appointment highlights the growing recognition of women's capabilities in commanding critical operational roles in the military.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Armed Forces Transfusion Centre (AFTC):**

 
 
• The AFTC is responsible for the collection, testing, storage, and distribution of blood and blood products for the Armed Forces.
 
• It operates under strict quality standards to ensure safe and efficient blood transfusion services.
 
• The centre supports military hospitals and field units during peacetime and wartime operations.
 
 
 
• **Transfusion Medicine:**
 
 
• It is a specialized branch of medicine focused on the transfusion of blood and its components.
 
• Key areas include blood donation, compatibility testing, and the management of blood storage and supply.
 
• Advancements in transfusion medicine have significantly reduced the risks of transfusion-transmitted infections.
 
 
 
• **Women in the Armed Forces:**
 
 
• Women were first inducted into the Indian Armed Forces in **1992** in non-combat roles.
 
• Over the years, their participation has expanded to include combat support and operational roles.
 
• Recent policy changes have allowed women to take on leadership positions, such as commanding units and serving in combat roles.
 
 
 
• **Gender Equality in the Military:**
 
 
• The Indian government and Armed Forces have taken steps to increase women's representation, including granting them permanent commissions in various branches.
 
• These initiatives aim to break gender stereotypes and promote equality within the ranks.

questions.question: In which of the following classical dance forms are the actors' faces painted to symbolise the type of character they are playing?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathakali** is a classical dance-drama originating from **Kerala, India**, known for its elaborate costumes, detailed face makeup, and intricate gestures.
 
• In Kathakali, actors' faces are painted to represent different characters, with colors symbolizing **qualities such as virtue, evil, and heroism**.
 
• Green makeup (Pacha) is used for noble and heroic characters, while red (Tati) or black (Kari) represents evil or demonic characters.
 
• The dance form combines **music, vocal performance, and facial expressions** to narrate stories, often drawn from Hindu epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
• It employs a highly stylized language of **facial expressions (Navarasas)** and hand gestures (Mudras) to communicate emotions and ideas effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mudras:**

 
 
• Hand gestures, known as Mudras, are used extensively in Kathakali to convey the dialogue and narrative.
 
• There are around 24 basic Mudras, which can be combined to create hundreds of meanings.
 
 
 
• **Costumes:**
 
 
• Kathakali costumes are elaborate and include large headdresses, colorful skirts, and intricate jewelry.
 
• The grandeur of the attire enhances the visual appeal and aids in character distinction.
 
 
 
• **Navarasas:**
 
 
• Navarasas are the nine emotions expressed in Kathakali, including love, anger, courage, and fear.
 
• These emotions are portrayed through precise facial movements and eye expressions.
 
 
 
• **Chenda and Maddalam:**
 
 
• Traditional instruments like the Chenda (drum) and Maddalam are integral to Kathakali performances.
 
• The rhythmic beats set the pace and mood for the storytelling.
 
 
 
• **Training:**
 
 
• Kathakali requires rigorous training, focusing on body control, flexibility, and mastery of expressions.
 
• Practitioners often undergo years of disciplined practice under experienced gurus.

questions.question: In 1992, which organisation launched Self Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NABARD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **NABARD** (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) launched the **Self Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme (SHG-BLP)** in **1992**, which is considered the world's largest microfinance initiative.
 
• The programme aims to **link banks and Self Help Groups (SHGs)**, enabling financial inclusion and empowering rural households, especially women.
 
• **SHGs under this programme** pool savings from members and use these funds for internal lending. Once they demonstrate financial discipline, they are eligible for loans from banks.
 
• By **March 2022**, over **10 million SHGs** were linked to banks under this programme, benefiting around **100 million rural households**.
 
• The initiative focuses on fostering **sustainable livelihoods** and improving socio-economic conditions in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self Help Groups (SHGs):**

 
 
• SHGs are informal associations of 10-20 people, typically women, who come together to save small amounts and access credit to meet their needs.
 
• The concept of SHGs promotes **financial literacy**, peer support, and collective decision-making.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of SHG-Bank Linkage Programme:**
 
 
• The programme strives to **improve access to formal financial services** for rural poor.
 
• It aims to promote **self-employment and entrepreneurship** among rural households.
 
 
 
• **NABARD:**
 
 
• NABARD was established in **1982** under the recommendations of the **B. Sivaraman Committee**.
 
• It is India's apex development bank for financing agriculture and rural development.
 
• NABARD plays a pivotal role in rural credit planning and implementation of various government schemes.
 
 
 
• **Microfinance:**
 
 
• Microfinance refers to providing small loans and financial services to individuals or groups who lack access to traditional banking services.
 
• It is a critical tool for promoting **financial inclusion** and alleviating poverty.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Bhadaravi Poonam Mela organised every year in the Nilkanth Mahadev temple premises in Babra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4) Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bhadaravi Poonam Mela** is an annual festival held in the premises of the **Nilkanth Mahadev Temple in Babra, Gujarat**.
 
• This mela (fair) is celebrated with great enthusiasm, primarily during the auspicious occasion of **Bhadarvi Poonam**, which typically occurs in the Hindu month of Bhadrapada (August-September).
 
• Devotees from across Gujarat and neighboring states visit the temple to seek blessings of Lord Shiva during this fair.
 
• The fair is renowned for its vibrant cultural activities, including folk music, dance performances, and traditional rituals dedicated to Lord Shiva.
 
• The mela also serves as an important platform for showcasing local handicrafts, food, and other cultural elements unique to the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhadarvi Poonam:**

 
 
• It marks the full moon day in the Hindu month of Bhadrapada, which is considered auspicious for spiritual activities and temple visits.
 
• This day is significant in many parts of India for worshipping deities, especially Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati.
 
 
 
• **Nilkanth Mahadev Temple:**
 
 
• The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva, often referred to as Nilkanth (the blue-throated one).
 
• It is a major pilgrimage site in Babra, Gujarat, and attracts thousands of devotees during the fair.
 
 
 
• **Fairs and Festivals in Gujarat:**
 
 
• Gujarat is known for its vibrant fairs and festivals, such as Navratri, Rann Utsav, and Shamlaji Fair.
 
• These events highlight the state’s rich culture, traditions, and heritage.
 
 
 
• **Role of Cultural Fairs:**
 
 
• Cultural fairs like Bhadaravi Poonam Mela play a crucial role in preserving local traditions and fostering communal harmony.
 
• They also contribute to the local economy by promoting tourism and handicrafts.

questions.question: As per the Constitution (Ninety-First Amendment) Act, 2003, the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall NOT exceed:

options.text: 20% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
10% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
25% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Constitution (Ninety-First Amendment) Act, 2003** was enacted to prevent the proliferation of ministers and maintain efficiency in governance.
 
• According to this amendment, the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the **Union Council of Ministers**, shall not exceed **15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha**.
 
• This limit applies to both the Union and State Councils of Ministers, as per **Articles 75 and 164** of the Constitution.
 
• The amendment was introduced to curb unnecessary expansion of ministries, which often led to inefficiency and misuse of public funds.
 
• The limit ensures a streamlined executive branch, fostering accountability and good governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Background of the 91st Amendment:**

 
 
• Before this amendment, there were no constitutional limits on the size of the Council of Ministers, leading to frequent cabinet expansions.
 
• The amendment was introduced following recommendations from the **National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC)**.
 
 
 
• **Article 75:**
 
 
• Under Article 75(1A), the 91st Amendment added a clause limiting the size of the Union Council of Ministers.
 
• This restriction applies to the total membership of the Council, including the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **State-Level Provisions:**
 
 
• Article 164(1A) imposes a similar 15% cap on the size of the State Council of Ministers, based on the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly.
 
• A minimum of 12 ministers is permitted in smaller states to ensure effective governance.
 
 
 
• **Anti-Defection Measures:**
 
 
• The 91st Amendment also strengthened anti-defection provisions by disqualifying defectors from holding ministerial office.
 
• It removed the provision allowing defections by a one-third split in a party, making the two-thirds merger rule mandatory.

questions.question: Which of the following cities is known as the Steel City in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jamshedpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jamshedpur** is widely known as the "Steel City of India" due to the presence of **Tata Steel**, the first private sector steel plant in India, established in 1907 by Jamsetji Tata.
 
• The city is located in the state of **Jharkhand**, and it serves as a major industrial hub for steel production in the country.
 
• Jamshedpur is home to **one of Asia's largest steel plants**, which has significantly contributed to India's industrial development.
 
• The infrastructure of Jamshedpur, including planned roads, parks, and utilities, was designed to support industrial activities and improve the quality of life for its residents.
 
• The city is managed by Tata Steel under the **Jamshedpur Utilities and Services Company (JUSCO)**, ensuring high standards of civic amenities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tata Steel:**

 
 
• Tata Steel, formerly known as Tata Iron and Steel Company Limited (TISCO), is one of the largest steel-producing companies in the world.
 
• It was established in 1907 in Jamshedpur and marked the beginning of modern steel production in India.
 
• The company produces a wide range of steel products, including flat steel, long steel, and specialty steel used in automotive, construction, and engineering industries.
 
 
 
• **Jamsetji Tata:**
 
 
• Jamsetji Tata was the founder of the Tata Group and is often regarded as the "Father of Indian Industry."
 
• He envisioned the idea of setting up a steel plant in India, which eventually became Tata Steel in Jamshedpur.
 
 
 
• **Planned City:**
 
 
• Jamshedpur is one of the first planned industrial cities in India, with well-organized infrastructure and green spaces.
 
• The city includes attractions like Jubilee Park, Dimna Lake, and Tata Steel Zoological Park, enhancing its livability.
 
 
 
• **Steel Industry in India:**
 
 
• India is the second-largest producer of steel in the world, with major production hubs in states like Jharkhand, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh.
 
• The steel industry is a critical part of India's economy, contributing significantly to infrastructure and manufacturing sectors.

questions.question: Indian classical musician, Ustad Rashid Khan was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2022 for his contribution to which of the following music categories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindustani classical music**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ustad Rashid Khan is a renowned vocalist of **Hindustani classical music**, specifically known for his mastery over the **Kirana Gharana**.
 
• In 2022, he was awarded the prestigious **Padma Bhushan**, India's third-highest civilian award, for his contribution to Indian classical music.
 
• He is celebrated for his expertise in **Khayal**, a form of Hindustani classical vocal music, and his ability to blend tradition with modernity.
 
• Ustad Rashid Khan is also known for his performances of **Thumri**, a semi-classical genre, which showcases his versatility as a musician.
 
• He has been widely acclaimed for his soulful renditions and his innovative approach to **raag improvisations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustani Classical Music:**

 
 
• This is one of the two major traditions of Indian classical music, the other being **Carnatic music**.
 
• It primarily emphasizes improvisation and exploration of **raagas** (melodic frameworks).
 
• Key components include **Khayal, Dhrupad, Thumri, Tarana**, and **Tappa**.
 
 
 
• **Kirana Gharana:**
 
 
• A school of Hindustani music known for its emphasis on **slow tempo (vilambit laya)** and intricate note-by-note elaboration of ragas.
 
• It was founded by Ustad Abdul Karim Khan and Ustad Abdul Wahid Khan.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards:**
 
 
• The **Padma Bhushan** is the third-highest civilian award in India after the Padma Vibhushan and Bharat Ratna.
 
• It recognizes distinguished service of a high order in various fields such as art, literature, science, and public affairs.
 
 
 
• **Khayal:**
 
 
• A prominent genre in Hindustani classical music, characterized by its **improvisation** and freedom of expression.
 
• The word "Khayal" means "imagination," emphasizing creativity in performance.

questions.question: In a metro station, it was observed that on an average 20 people per minute were using the escalator to reach at a height of 15 metres. Calculate the power of the escalator assuming the average mass of people to be 50 kg and acceleration due to gravity to be 10 m/s².
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: 2.5 kW**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The escalator raises 20 people per minute to a height of 15 metres. Each person has an average mass of 50 kg.
 
• The gravitational force acting on each person is calculated as **weight = mass × gravity**, which is 50 kg × 10 m/s² = 500 N.
 
• The work done to raise one person is **work = force × height**, which is 500 N × 15 m = 7500 J.
 
• For 20 people, the total work done per minute is 7500 J × 20 = 150,000 J.
 
• Power is calculated as **power = work done / time**. Since time is 60 seconds (1 minute), the power of the escalator is 150,000 J / 60 s = 2500 W or 2.5 kW.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Work:** In physics, work is defined as the product of force applied and displacement in the direction of the force. It is measured in joules (J).
 
• **Power:** Power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred. The unit of power is watts (W), where 1 watt = 1 joule/second.
 
• **Gravitational Force:** The force exerted by gravity on an object is calculated as mass × acceleration due to gravity (g), which is approximately 9.8 m/s² but rounded to 10 m/s² for simplification.
 
• **Energy Conversion:** In machines like escalators, mechanical energy is used to lift objects or people against gravity, converting electrical energy into mechanical energy.
 
• **Efficiency:** Practical escalators may have less efficiency due to friction and other factors, but theoretical calculations assume ideal conditions.

questions.question: When was the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar, an award given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi to outstanding artists under 40 who have demonstrated talent in the fields of music, dance and theatre, started?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2006**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar** was instituted by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi** in the year **2006**.
 
• This award is given to talented artists under the age of **40** in the fields of **music, dance, and theatre**.
 
• The award aims to recognize and promote young talent in India’s **performing arts** landscape.
 
• Recipients of this award are selected based on their outstanding contributions and promising performances in their respective fields.
 
• The **Sangeet Natak Akademi** is India's national academy for music, dance, and drama, established in **1952**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ustad Bismillah Khan:**

 
 
• He was a legendary **shehnai maestro** and one of India's most celebrated classical musicians.
 
• Bismillah Khan received India's highest civilian award, the **Bharat Ratna**, in **2001**.
 
• His contributions to Indian classical music have left an indelible mark on the cultural heritage of the nation.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi:**
 
 
• It is an autonomous organization under the **Ministry of Culture**, Government of India.
 
• The Akademi is responsible for the preservation and promotion of India's cultural heritage in the performing arts.
 
• It organizes festivals, awards, and training programs to nurture and support artists.
 
 
 
• **Categories of Performing Arts:**
 
 
• Performing arts include various forms of art such as **music, dance, drama, and theatre**.
 
• These art forms are integral to India's rich and diverse cultural traditions.
 
 
 
• **Other Awards by Sangeet Natak Akademi:**
 
 
• The Akademi also presents the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship**, **Akademi Awards**, and organizes various scholarships for artists.
 
• These awards aim to honor exemplary contributions in the field of performing arts.

questions.question: Who among the following was the pioneer of 'Bhoodan Movement'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acharya Vinoba Bhave**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Acharya Vinoba Bhave** was the pioneer of the **Bhoodan Movement**, which aimed at redistributing land to landless farmers.
 
• The movement began in **1951** at Pochampally village in Telangana, where Vinoba Bhave persuaded wealthy landowners to donate land for the poor.
 
• The term "Bhoodan" translates to "**Land Donation**" and was a non-violent initiative inspired by Gandhian philosophy.
 
• Vinoba Bhave walked across villages, requesting landowners to donate a part of their land voluntarily to the landless, promoting **social equality**.
 
• By 1954, the movement expanded into the **Gramdan Movement**, where entire villages donated land for community welfare.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vinoba Bhave** was a spiritual leader and a prominent disciple of Mahatma Gandhi, deeply committed to the principles of non-violence and selfless service.
 
• The **Bhoodan Movement** was a part of larger Gandhian efforts to address rural poverty and land inequality in post-independence India.
 
• The movement significantly influenced the concept of **land reforms** in India, although its success varied across regions.
 
• The **Gramdan Movement**, derived from Bhoodan, aimed to promote collective ownership of land and community-driven development.
 
• Vinoba Bhave received the **Ramon Magsaysay Award** for his social and leadership efforts in 1958.

questions.question: In Dholavira, which of the following materials is extensively used as a building material?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dholavira, one of the most prominent archaeological sites of the Indus Valley Civilization, extensively utilized **stone** as a primary building material.
 
• The city’s structures, including walls, reservoirs, and gateways, were constructed using locally available stone, especially **sandstone and limestone**.
 
• Unlike other Harappan sites that predominantly used bricks, Dholavira is unique for its reliance on stone due to its geographical location in the arid region of Gujarat.
 
• The use of stone ensured durability and adaptability to the harsh climate of the Rann of Kutch, where Dholavira is located.
 
• The site’s sophisticated water management system, including reservoirs and drains, was also carved from stone, showcasing advanced engineering techniques of the Harappan people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dholavira:**

 
 
• Dholavira is located in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat, and is one of the largest Harappan settlements in India.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized for its unique urban planning and water conservation systems.
 
 
 
• **Water Management System:**
 
 
• Dholavira is famous for its intricate water management system, including reservoirs, step wells, and drains.
 
• This system reflects the ingenuity of the Harappan civilization in adapting to a water-scarce environment.
 
 
 
• **Harappan Architecture:**
 
 
• The Harappan civilization is known for its urban planning, including grid-patterned streets, drainage systems, and standardized building materials like bricks and stones.
 
 
 
• **Materials Used in Harappan Sites:**
 
 
• While baked and unbaked bricks were common in most Harappan sites, Dholavira stands out for its extensive use of stone due to the availability of local resources.
 
• Other materials used included wood and mud for specific purposes like roofing and insulation.

questions.question: The concept of Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Australia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of the **Concurrent List** in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the **Australian Constitution**.
 
• In the **Australian federal system**, powers are divided between the federal and state governments, with concurrent powers allowing both levels of government to legislate on certain subjects.
 
• The Indian Constitution adopts this idea to allocate legislative powers between the Union and State legislatures under **Article 246** and the **Seventh Schedule**.
 
• The Concurrent List in India contains subjects on which both the Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate, but in case of a conflict, the Union law prevails (as per **Article 254**).
 
• Examples of subjects in the Concurrent List include education, forest, trade unions, and marriage laws.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution**:

 
 
• The Seventh Schedule divides legislative powers between the Union and State governments into three lists: **Union List, State List, and Concurrent List**.
 
• The Union List contains 100 subjects, the State List has 61 subjects, and the Concurrent List has 52 subjects as of the latest amendment.
 
 
 
• **Article 246**:
 
 
• It lays down the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States.
 
• Parliament has exclusive power to make laws on subjects in the Union List, while State Legislatures have exclusive power on the State List.
 
 
 
• **Article 254**:
 
 
• In case of a conflict between Union and State laws on a Concurrent List subject, the law made by the Union Parliament will prevail.
 
• However, a state law can prevail if it has received the President's assent.
 
 
 
• **Federal Features of the Indian Constitution**:
 
 
• Indian federalism is unique, combining the division of powers with a strong unitary bias.
 
• Features like a strong central government, single citizenship, and a unified judiciary distinguish it from purely federal systems like the USA.

questions.question: What is the rank of Sri Lanka in the Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3 (60)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sri Lanka ranked **60th out of 125 countries** in the **Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2023**, indicating a moderate level of hunger.
 
• The **Global Hunger Index** measures hunger and undernutrition across the world, using four key indicators: undernourishment, child wasting, child stunting, and child mortality.
 
• Sri Lanka’s score on the GHI 2023 was **13.0**, which falls in the "moderate" category on the hunger severity scale.
 
• Despite challenges such as economic instability and food insecurity, Sri Lanka has shown a relatively better ranking in comparison to many South Asian countries.
 
• The **Global Hunger Index** is jointly published by **Concern Worldwide** and **Welthungerhilfe**, which assess hunger comprehensively using internationally recognized data.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Hunger Index (GHI):**

 
 
• The GHI is an annual report designed to track hunger globally, regionally, and by country.
 
• It uses a 100-point scale where 0 represents no hunger and 100 represents the worst level of hunger.
 
• The GHI focuses on four indicators: undernourishment, child wasting (low weight for height), child stunting (low height for age), and child mortality.
 
 
 
• **Hunger Severity Categories:**
 
 
• GHI scores are divided into five categories: low (≤9.9), moderate (10.0–19.9), serious (20.0–34.9), alarming (35.0–49.9), and extremely alarming (≥50.0).
 
• Sri Lanka’s score of 13.0 places it in the "moderate" hunger category.
 
 
 
• **South Asia and Hunger:**
 
 
• South Asia is one of the worst-performing regions in the GHI due to widespread food insecurity, poverty, and undernutrition.
 
• Countries like India, Pakistan, and Afghanistan rank lower than Sri Lanka in the 2023 GHI.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Sri Lanka:**
 
 
• Sri Lanka faces challenges like economic crises, inflation, and disruptions in food supply chains, which contribute to food insecurity.
 
• Despite these, the country has shown progress in reducing child malnutrition and improving food accessibility.

questions.question: What is the primary acid found in citrus fruits like oranges and lemons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Citric acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Citric acid** is the primary acid found in citrus fruits like oranges, lemons, limes, and grapefruits.
 
• It gives these fruits their characteristic tangy and sour flavor.
 
• Citric acid is a weak organic acid with the chemical formula **C₆H₈O₇**.
 
• This acid plays a crucial role in the **citric acid cycle (Krebs cycle)**, a key metabolic pathway in living organisms.
 
• It is widely used in the food and beverage industry as a natural preservative and flavor enhancer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lactic acid:** Found in sour milk products like yogurt and responsible for muscle fatigue during intense physical activity.
 
• **Tartaric acid:** Found naturally in grapes and bananas; used in baking powder as a leavening agent.
 
• **Acetic acid:** The primary component of vinegar, giving it its distinctive sharp odor and taste.
 
• Citrus fruits are an excellent source of vitamin C (**ascorbic acid**), which supports immune health and acts as an antioxidant.
 
• Citric acid has applications beyond food, including in cleaning products, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics due to its chelating and pH-regulating properties.

questions.question: In which state are the Gua and Noamundi iron ore mines located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2) Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gua and Noamundi mines are located in the state of **Jharkhand**, India.
 
• Noamundi is a major iron ore mining town in West Singhbhum district of Jharkhand, managed by **Tata Steel**.
 
• Gua is another important mining area in West Singhbhum district, known for its high-grade **iron ore reserves**.
 
• Both these regions are part of the **Chotanagpur Plateau**, which is rich in mineral resources including iron ore, coal, and mica.
 
• Jharkhand contributes significantly to India's iron ore production, making it a key player in the country's steel and mining industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron Ore:**

 
 
• Iron ore is one of the most abundant minerals on Earth, primarily used for making steel.
 
• The major types of iron ore include hematite (high iron content) and magnetite.
 
• India is among the top producers of iron ore, and the mineral plays a vital role in the country's economy.
 
 
 
• **Chotanagpur Plateau:**
 
 
• This plateau is the mineral-rich region of eastern India, covering parts of Jharkhand, Odisha, and West Bengal.
 
• It is often referred to as the "mineral heartland of India."
 
 
 
• **Mining in Jharkhand:**
 
 
• Jharkhand has over 40% of India's mineral resources.
 
• Besides iron ore, the state is rich in coal, uranium, copper, mica, and bauxite.
 
 
 
• **Tata Steel and Mining:**
 
 
• Tata Steel has been operating in Noamundi since 1925, making it one of India's oldest mining operations.
 
• The company is involved in sustainable mining practices to reduce environmental impact.

questions.question: The climatic diversity of India is characterised by its distinctiveness, and one of the following factors does NOT contribute to it is ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1 (Longitudinal extent)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Longitudinal extent** does not significantly influence climatic diversity in India as it mainly determines the local time differences across the country, rather than climatic variations.
 
• The climate variations across India are majorly influenced by factors like latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, and geographical features such as mountains and plateaus.
 
• India’s latitudinal extent (between 8° N and 37° N) contributes to the climatic diversity by placing the country in both tropical and subtropical zones.
 
• Topography, including the Himalayas and the Thar Desert, plays a critical role in influencing climatic patterns, such as monsoons and regional temperature differences.
 
• Vegetation impacts local climates by affecting moisture levels, temperature regulation, and precipitation patterns, contributing to India’s climatic diversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Latitude and Climate:**

 
 
• India’s latitudinal extent ensures climatic zones ranging from tropical in the south to subtropical and temperate in the north.
 
• Regions near the Equator experience higher temperatures and greater humidity compared to regions farther north.
 
 
 
• **Role of Topography:**
 
 
• The Himalayas prevent cold Central Asian winds from entering India, contributing to the tropical climate in most parts of the country.
 
• Western Ghats and coastal areas experience high rainfall due to orographic rainfall during monsoons.
 
 
 
• **Vegetation and Climate:**
 
 
• Dense forests in regions like the Western Ghats and Northeast India contribute to higher rainfall and cooler climates.
 
• Deforestation in some areas has led to changes in local climates, including increased aridity and temperature.
 
 
 
• **Longitude and Time Zones:**
 
 
• The longitudinal extent of India (68°7' E to 97°25' E) results in a time difference of nearly 2 hours between its eastern and western extremities.
 
• However, longitude has minimal impact on climatic diversity as it does not directly influence temperature, precipitation, or seasonal patterns.

questions.question: The rock-cut temple of Shiva built by Krishna I is found at which of the following places?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ellora**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The rock-cut temple of Shiva built by Krishna I is the famous **Kailasa Temple at Ellora**, located in Maharashtra, India.
 
• This temple is part of the **Ellora Caves**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site comprising 34 rock-cut monasteries and temples.
 
• The Kailasa Temple is a monolithic structure, meaning it was carved out of a single rock, showcasing **remarkable ancient Indian rock-cut architecture.**
 
• Krishna I, a ruler of the Rashtrakuta dynasty, commissioned this temple in the **8th century CE**.
 
• The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is designed to represent Mount Kailasa, the mythical abode of Shiva.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ellora Caves:**

 
 
• Ellora houses a total of 34 caves, divided into three groups: 12 Buddhist caves, 17 Hindu caves, and 5 Jain caves, symbolizing religious harmony in ancient India.
 
• The caves were excavated between the 6th and 10th centuries CE and exhibit the architectural brilliance of their respective religious traditions.
 
 
 
• **Rashtrakuta Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Rashtrakutas were a powerful dynasty that ruled large parts of the Indian subcontinent between the 6th and 10th centuries CE.
 
• They were known for their patronage of art, architecture, and literature, with the Kailasa Temple being one of their most notable contributions.
 
 
 
• **Kailasa Temple Design:**
 
 
• The temple is designed in the **Dravidian style** of architecture, featuring intricate carvings, sculptures, and depictions of Hindu mythology.
 
• The construction involved removing over 200,000 tons of rock, an engineering feat that continues to awe historians and archaeologists.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Status:**
 
 
• The Ellora Caves were recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983 for their exceptional cultural and historical significance.
 
• They attract millions of tourists and researchers every year, making them one of the most iconic heritage sites in India.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements in the context of the Vedas.

1. The Vedas are called Shruti.

2. The Rigveda consists of ten Mandalas.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The Vedas are known as Shruti:** The term "Shruti" means "that which is heard" and refers to the oral transmission of the Vedas, emphasizing their divine origin.
 
• **The Rigveda consists of ten Mandalas:** The Rigveda, the oldest of the four Vedas, is divided into ten Mandalas (books), containing hymns dedicated to various deities.
 
• The Rigveda is considered one of the most ancient religious texts in the world, composed around 1500–1200 BCE.
 
• Both these statements highlight the foundational nature of the Vedas in Indian religious and philosophical traditions.
 
• The Vedas, including the Rigveda, are regarded as apauruṣeya (not of human agency) and are central to Vedic literature and Hinduism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Four Vedas:** The Vedas consist of four texts: Rigveda (hymns), Yajurveda (sacrificial rituals), Samaveda (melody and chants), and Atharvaveda (spells and charms).
 
• **Rigveda Structure:** It is divided into Mandalas, which are further subdivided into hymns (Suktas) composed in praise of deities like Agni, Indra, and Varuna.
 
• **Oral Tradition:** The Vedas were transmitted orally for centuries before being written down, with rigorous methods to preserve their accuracy.
 
• **Language:** The Vedas are composed in Vedic Sanskrit, an ancient form of the Sanskrit language.
 
• **Philosophical Significance:** The Vedas form the basis of Vedic philosophy, rituals, and spirituality, influencing Indian culture and thought deeply.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides provision for appointment of the same person as the Governor for two or more states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 153**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 153** of the Constitution of India provides for the position of the Governor in each state.
 
• This Article allows the **appointment of the same individual as Governor for two or more states**.
 
• The Governor is appointed by the **President of India** and holds office during the President's pleasure.
 
• The provision for one Governor serving multiple states helps in administrative efficiency and cost-effectiveness.
 
• For example, a single Governor serves the states of **Punjab, Haryana, and the Union Territory of Chandigarh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor's Role**: The Governor acts as the constitutional head of the state, functioning as a link between the state government and the central government.
 
• **Article 157**: It lays down the qualifications required to be appointed as a Governor, such as being a citizen of India and at least 35 years of age.
 
• **Article 158**: It specifies the conditions of the Governor's office, including that the Governor should not hold any other office of profit.
 
• **Dual Role of Governor**: In case of a single Governor for multiple states, the individual must address the unique needs and challenges of each state while upholding constitutional provisions.
 
• **Special Provisions**: The President of India, while appointing a Governor for multiple states, ensures that the decision aligns with the administrative and political requirements of the region.

questions.question: In which of the following year did India win the ICC T20 Men's Cricket World Cup?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2007**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India won the inaugural ICC T20 Men's Cricket World Cup in **2007**, held in South Africa.
 
• The final match was played on **24th September 2007**, where India defeated **Pakistan** by 5 runs.
 
• The tournament was notable for introducing the **Super Over** and other innovations to the T20 format of cricket.
 
• **MS Dhoni** captained the Indian cricket team, marking his first major tournament as a leader.
 
• The final saw **Joginder Sharma** bowling the last over, securing India's victory with a decisive wicket.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Format of ICC T20 World Cup:**

 
 
• The ICC T20 World Cup is played in the **T20 format**, where each team plays a maximum of 20 overs per innings.
 
• The tournament includes a combination of **group stages**, **Super 8**, and knockout rounds such as semi-finals and finals.
 
 
 
• **Performance of Key Players in 2007:**
 
 
• **Yuvraj Singh** hit six sixes in an over against England in the Super 8 stage, creating a record.
 
• **Gautam Gambhir** was the top scorer in the final, scoring 75 runs off 54 balls.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Victory:**
 
 
• This win established India as a dominant force in the T20 cricket format.
 
• The victory also boosted the popularity of T20 cricket in India, paving the way for the launch of the **Indian Premier League (IPL)** in 2008.
 
 
 
• **Other Highlights of the 2007 Tournament:**
 
 
• A total of **12 teams** participated in the tournament, including Test-playing nations and associate members.
 
• The tournament saw several thrilling matches, including a **bowl-out** between India and Pakistan during the group stage.

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)

questions.question: How many titles did West Bengal win in the Santosh Trophy events up to the 2022-23 season?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3 (32)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• West Bengal has won the prestigious **Santosh Trophy** a record **32 times** up to the 2022-23 season.
 
• The state has been a dominant force in Indian football, with its first title victory dating back to **1941**.
 
• West Bengal's most recent triumph in the Santosh Trophy came in the **2016-17 season**, defeating Goa 1-0 in the final.
 
• West Bengal has consistently showcased its footballing prowess by producing numerous talented players who have represented India at various levels.
 
• The Santosh Trophy is considered one of the most prestigious football tournaments for state and institutional teams in India, organized by the **All India Football Federation (AIFF)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Santosh Trophy Overview:**

 
 
• Established in **1941**, it is an annual football competition in India.
 
• The tournament is named after **Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhary of Santosh**, who was the President of the Indian Football Association (IFA).
 
 
 
• **Format of the Tournament:**
 
 
• Teams from Indian states, union territories, and government institutions participate in the competition.
 
• The format includes group stages followed by knockout rounds, culminating in the final.
 
 
 
• **All India Football Federation (AIFF):**
 
 
• It is the governing body for football in India, established in **1937**.
 
• The AIFF oversees the organization of major football tournaments in the country, including the Santosh Trophy.
 
 
 
• **Other Key Performers:**
 
 
• Kerala and Punjab are other top-performing teams in the Santosh Trophy, each with multiple titles.
 
• Kerala has won the tournament **6 times**, while Punjab has secured victory **8 times**.

questions.question: Who among the following Governor-Generals declared 'Sati' practice as illegal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord William Bentinck**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord William Bentinck, the Governor-General of India from 1828 to 1835, declared the practice of **Sati illegal and punishable by law** in 1829.
 
• The regulation abolishing Sati was officially titled **Regulation XVII** and was passed on December 4, 1829.
 
• Bentinck's decision was influenced by strong opposition to Sati from reformers like **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**, who advocated for women's rights and called Sati a barbaric practice.
 
• The abolition applied to the territories under the control of the East India Company, including Bengal, Madras, and Bombay presidencies.
 
• The regulation classified Sati as culpable homicide, thereby making those involved in enforcing or facilitating the practice legally accountable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sati Practice:**

 
 
• Sati was a funeral practice in which a widow immolated herself on her husband's funeral pyre.
 
• It was prevalent in certain parts of India and was often enforced due to social and religious pressures.
 
 
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy's Role:**
 
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy, a prominent social reformer, campaigned extensively against Sati.
 
• He highlighted the inhuman nature of the practice and used religious texts to argue against its legitimacy.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Ban:**
 
 
• The abolition of Sati was a significant step in the direction of women's rights and social reform in India.
 
• It marked the beginning of a series of reforms aimed at curbing oppressive practices against women.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Lord William Bentinck:**
 
 
• Bentinck is remembered as a reformist Governor-General who introduced several progressive policies, including the abolition of Sati and efforts to suppress Thuggee.
 
• His tenure laid the foundation for modern social reforms in colonial India.

questions.question: Which of the following fictional towns is mentioned in the English novel 'In Custody' written by Anita Desai?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mirpore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mirpore** is the fictional town mentioned in Anita Desai's novel *In Custody*.
 
• The novel revolves around the life of a Hindi lecturer, Deven Sharma, who is sent to interview Nur, a declining Urdu poet in Mirpore.
 
• Through Mirpore, the author vividly portrays the socio-cultural environment of a small, decaying town in India.
 
• The setting of Mirpore serves as a backdrop to explore themes like linguistic identity, cultural deterioration, and personal conflicts.
 
• Anita Desai’s use of Mirpore reflects the disintegration of the poetic Urdu culture amidst modernity and changing societal dynamics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anita Desai:**

 
 
• Anita Desai is a renowned Indian author known for her introspective and culturally rich literary works.
 
• She has been shortlisted three times for the Booker Prize and was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award for her novel *Fire on the Mountain*.
 
 
 
• **In Custody:**
 
 
• *In Custody* was published in 1984 and explores themes of loss, linguistic identity, and cultural conflict.
 
• The novel was adapted into a film by Ismail Merchant in 1993, starring Shashi Kapoor, Om Puri, and Shabana Azmi.
 
 
 
• **Urdu Poetry and Culture:**
 
 
• The novel emphasizes the decline of Urdu poetry and its cultural significance in a modernizing India.
 
• Nur, the Urdu poet in the story, symbolizes the fading glory of a rich literary tradition.
 
 
 
• **Kanthapura and Malgudi:**
 
 
• Kanthapura is a fictional village in Raja Rao's novel *Kanthapura*, depicting the Gandhian freedom struggle.
 
• Malgudi is the fictional South Indian town created by R.K. Narayan in his series of novels and short stories.

questions.question: A particular cell present in the excretory system of flatworms, which helps them removing waste materials is the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**flame cell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Flame cells** are specialized excretory cells found in flatworms, such as Planaria, belonging to the phylum Platyhelminthes.
 
• These cells play a crucial role in the removal of nitrogenous waste products and maintaining osmotic balance in flatworms.
 
• Flame cells are part of the **protonephridial system**, which functions as the excretory system in these organisms.
 
• The name "flame cell" is derived from the flickering movement of cilia present inside the cell, resembling a flame.
 
• The cilia in flame cells drive the waste materials and excess water out of the body through excretory pores.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protonephridial System:**

 
 
• This system consists of a network of tubules and flame cells that facilitate excretion and osmoregulation in flatworms.
 
• It is considered a primitive excretory structure compared to advanced systems in higher organisms.
 
 
 
• **Flatworms (Platyhelminthes):**
 
 
• Flatworms are bilaterally symmetrical, dorsoventrally flattened, and lack a circulatory system.
 
• They rely on diffusion for nutrient and gas exchange, making their excretory system essential for waste removal.
 
 
 
• **Cnidoblast Cells:**
 
 
• These are specialized cells found in cnidarians (e.g., jellyfish) and are used for defense and prey capture, not excretion.
 
 
 
• **Osmoregulation in Flatworms:**
 
 
• Flame cells are pivotal in regulating the water content of the organism, ensuring it maintains homeostasis in aquatic environments.
